chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever buys something that has a defect or a flaw which he was not released from, and he was not released from it, and he made something new in it after he took possession of it, and he knew of that flaw or that defect, then the sale is confirmed upon him, and he is returned an amount equal to what that disease and defect reduce from the price of that [item] had it not had it."

key_terms.عَيْبٌ: defect or flaw in an item

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a sale when a hidden defect is discovered after purchase?
ai.summary: Reported from Imam al-Baqir (AS) and transmitted via the reliable chain of Zurarah, this hadith clarifies the distinction between 'ayb' (defect) and 'awar' (flaw) in commercial transactions, affirming the validity of the sale while mandating a proportional deduction (kaffar) for the buyer. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness and transparency, ensuring that sellers compensate for hidden imperfections that diminish the item's utility or value.
